name: 4000 Essential English Words
description: 3600 từ vựng tiếng Anh thiết yếu với định nghĩa và câu ví dụ tiếng Anh — phù hợp người học ở mọi trình độ

words.definition: To agree is to have the same opinion or belief as another person.
words.example: The students agree they have too much homework.

words.definition: Alcohol is a type of drink that can make people drunk.
words.example: A person should not drive a car after he or she has been drinking alcohol.

words.definition: To arrive is to get somewhere.
words.example: They arrived at school at 7 a.m.

words.definition: August is the eighth month of the year.
words.example: Is your birthday in August?

words.definition: A boat is a vehicle that moves across water.
words.example: There is a small boat on the lake.

words.definition: Breakfast is the morning meal.
words.example: I ate eggs for breakfast.

words.definition: A camera is a piece of equipment that takes pictures.
words.example: I brought my camera on my vacation.

words.definition: A capital is a city where a country’s government is based.
words.example: The capital of the United States is Washington, D.C.

words.definition: To catch is to grab or get something.
words.example: Did you catch the ball during the baseball game?

words.definition: A duck is a small water bird.
words.example: People feed ducks at the lake.

words.definition: To enjoy is to like something.
words.example: The woman enjoys riding her bicycle.

words.definition: To invite is to ask someone to come to a place or event.
words.example: I will invite my friends to my birthday party.

words.definition: To love is to like something or someone a lot.
words.example: I love my family very much.

words.definition: A month is one of 12 periods of time in one year.
words.example: January is the first month of the year.

words.definition: To travel is to go to a faraway place on vacation or business.
words.example: They will travel to Argentina this summer.

words.definition: If something is typical, it is normal, or something that usually happens.
words.example: My typical breakfast is toast and eggs.

words.definition: To visit is to go and spend time in another place or see another person.
words.example: She wants to visit her grandmother.

words.definition: Weather is the temperature and the state of the outdoors.
words.example: Today’s weather is rainy and cloudy.

words.definition: A week is a period of time that is seven days long.
words.example: What are you doing next week?

words.definition: Wine is an alcoholic drink made from grapes.
words.example: The store carried both red and white wine.

words.definition: An adventure is a fun or exciting thing that you do.
words.example: Riding in the rough water was an adventure.

words.definition: To approach something means to move close to it.
words.example: The boy approached his school.

words.definition: Carefully means with great attention, especially to detail or safety.
words.example: The baby carefully climbed down the stairs.

words.definition: A chemical is something that scientists use in chemistry.
words.example: The scientist mixed the chemicals.

words.definition: To create means to make something new.
words.example: She created an igloo from blocks of snow.

words.definition: Evil describes something or someone bad or cruel, not good.
words.example: They felt a strange, evil presence as they got closer to the house.

words.definition: An experiment is a test that you do to see what will happen.
words.example: The student did an experiment in science class.

words.definition: To kill someone or something is to make them die.
words.example: I killed the fly.

words.definition: A laboratory is a room where a scientist works.
words.example: My mother works in a laboratory.

words.definition: Laugh is the sound made when someone is happy or a funny thing occurs.
words.example: The sound of her laugh filled the room.

words.definition: If a sound is loud, it is strong and very easy to hear.
words.example: The man’s voice was so loud that we all could hear him.

words.definition: When a person is nervous, they think something bad will happen.
words.example: The boy became nervous when he heard the news.

words.definition: A noise is an unpleasant sound.
words.example: The crying baby made a loud noise.

words.definition: A project is a type of work that you do for school or a job.
words.example: His afternoon work project was to paint the room green.

words.definition: To scare someone is to make them feel afraid.
words.example: My uncle was scared by what he saw in the room.

words.definition: A secret is something that you do not tell other people.
words.example: The two boys were sharing a secret.

words.definition: To shout is to say something loudly.
words.example: My boss shouted at me because I was late for work.

words.definition: To smell something means to use your nose to sense it.
words.example: The two friends smelled the flower.

words.definition: If something is terrible, it is very bad.
words.example: The way he treated his classmate was terrible.

words.definition: If something is worse, it is of poorer quality than another thing.
words.example: Business was worse this month than last month.

words.definition: An alien is a creature from a different world.
words.example: The alien came in peace.

words.definition: If you are among certain things, they are all around you.
words.example: There was a red apple among the green ones.

words.definition: A chart is a list of information.
words.example: We used a chart to see how we had improved.

words.definition: A cloud is a group of water drops in the sky.
words.example: The sky was filled with white clouds.

words.definition: To describe is to say or write what someone or something is like.
words.example: They described their tree as colorful, with gold ribbon and a star.

words.definition: Ever means at any time.
words.example: Going skiing last winter was the most fun I’ve ever had.

words.definition: To fail means you do not succeed in what you try to do.
words.example: Since he failed to get the job, he was sad.

words.definition: A grade is a score or mark given to someone’s work.
words.example: I managed to get good grades on my report card.

words.definition: Instead means in place of.
words.example: He ate the carrot instead of the ice cream.

words.definition: A library is a place where you go to read books.
words.example: The library at school is full of books.

words.definition: I like taking photographs.
words.example: I took this photograph with my cell phone.

words.definition: A planet is a large round thing in space.
words.example: Saturn is the planet with the ring around it.

words.definition: A report is something someone writes for school or work.
words.example: Karen had trouble writing her report.

words.definition: Several is more than two but not many.
words.example: He had to read several books for class.

words.definition: An object’s shape is the arrangement of its sides and surfaces.
words.example: Even with your eyes closed you can feel the shape of it.

words.definition: To solve something is to find an answer to it.
words.example: All the students could easily solve the math problem.

words.definition: If something happens suddenly, it happens quickly and unexpectedly.
words.example: I was surprised when my friends suddenly shouted, “Happy birthday!”

words.definition: To suppose is to guess.
words.example: I suppose I should go home now.

words.definition: To understand something you need to know what it means.
words.example: Henry could not understand the message.

words.definition: To view is to look at something.
words.example: Michael likes to view himself in the mirror.

words.definition: When a thing is appropriate, it is right or normal.
words.example: It’s appropriate to wear a suit when you go to the office.

words.definition: To avoid something is to stay away from it.
words.example: Avoid the broken bottle on the floor.

words.definition: To behave is to act in a particular way, especially to be good.
words.example: She always behaves well when her father is around.

words.definition: When someone is calm, they do not get excited or upset.
words.example: A nice warm bath makes me feel so calm.

words.definition: Concern is a feeling of worry.
words.example: I was filled with concern after reading the newspaper.

words.definition: To be content is to be happy and not want more.
words.example: The baby looked very content sitting on the floor.

words.definition: If you expect something to happen, you believe it will happen.
words.example: I expect the bus to be here very soon.

words.definition: When something happens frequently, it happens often.
words.example: We meet frequently, either at the beginning or end of the week.

words.definition: A habit is a thing that you do often.
words.example: Smoking is a bad habit that can kill you.

words.definition: To instruct is to teach.
words.example: My teacher instructs us in several subjects.

words.definition: An issue is an important topic.
words.example: The men spoke about issues that were important to the people.

words.definition: None means not any of something.
words.example: He spent all his money. There is none left.

words.definition: If people are patient, they don’t become angry or upset easily.
words.example: I had to be patient and wait until 5 o’clock to leave.

words.definition: If something is positive, it is good.
words.example: She has a positive future ahead of her after finishing college.

words.definition: To punish means to make someone suffer for breaking the rules or laws.
words.example: To punish me, my teacher had me stand in the corner.

words.definition: To represent is to speak or act for a person or group.
words.example: My lawyer will represent me in court.

words.definition: To shake is to move back and forth or up and down quickly.
words.example: When people shake hands, it usually means they agree.

words.definition: To spread is to move out to cover a larger area.
words.example: I like to spread butter on my toast.

words.definition: To stroll means to walk slowly and calmly.
words.example: My dog and I strolled through the park today.

words.definition: A village is a very small town.
words.example: There are only a few houses in my village.

words.definition: When someone is active, they move a lot or have a lot of things to do.
words.example: It is important to be active and not sit around all the time.

words.definition: An adult is a person who is more than 18 years old.
words.example: My mom and dad are adults.

words.definition: Age is how many years someone has lived.
words.example: She died at the age of 80.

words.definition: When something is bad, it is not good.
words.example: She is unhappy because she had a bad day.

words.definition: Balance is when two or more things are equal.
words.example: A good balance between work and fun helps keep you healthy.

words.definition: A bike is a vehicle with two wheels powered by a human.
words.example: He rides his bike to school every day.

words.definition: To choose is to pick something or make a decision.
words.example: I have to choose between taking art classes and sports lessons.

words.definition: A doctor is a person who studies medicine and helps sick people.
words.example: You should go to the doctor when you are sick.

words.definition: During an event means while the event was happening.
words.example: Did you sleep during the movie?

words.definition: Football is a sport with eleven members and an oval-shaped ball.
words.example: Football is a popular sport in the United States.

words.definition: When something is fun, it is enjoyable.
words.example: We had a fun time at the birthday party.

words.definition: A game is an activity where people compete against each other.
words.example: Let’s play a board game tonight.

words.definition: A heart is an organ that keeps the body alive.
words.example: My heart beats fast when I am nervous.

words.definition: Golf is a sport with clubs and a small white ball.
words.example: People play golf in nice weather.

words.definition: To increase is to make something larger.
words.example: I will increase my score if I study for the test.

words.definition: Life is the time when a person is alive.
words.example: My grandfather had a long life.

words.definition: A kilometer is a unit of measurement that is 1,000 meters.
words.example: A marathon is 42.2 kilometers.

words.definition: Often is when something happens many times.
words.example: He often goes to bed early during the week.

words.definition: If you have plenty of something, there is a lot of it.
words.example: We have plenty of fruit, so help yourself.

words.definition: Weight is how heavy something or someone is.
words.example: I gained weight because I ate a lot of pizza.

words.definition: When people or things are apart, they are not next to each other.
words.example: They moved apart and then came back together.

words.definition: An attribute is a characteristic of a person or thing.
words.example: He isn’t very clever, but he does have some other positive attributes.

words.definition: A bilingual person can speak two languages.
words.example: Since you already know English, after learning French you’ll be bilingual.

words.definition: Something completely different is very, very different from before.
words.example: I was completely wrong.

words.definition: To dash means to run or move quickly.
words.example: Helen dashed up the stairs so she wouldn’t be late for her appointment.

words.definition: Disgust is a feeling of distaste and anger caused by something rude or unpleasant.
words.example: He felt disgust toward his date because she had such terrible eating habits.

words.definition: Something fashionable is what people like to wear and do now.
words.example: It is very fashionable to wear a hat.

words.definition: Something foreign is something we are not used to.
words.example: He has travelled widely in foreign countries.

words.definition: A gulf is a gap between people who do not understand each other.
words.example: There has been a gulf between James and Tony since their parents died.

words.definition: A mirror is usually made of glass, and you can see yourself in it.
words.example: He used the mirror to shine light in their eyes.

words.definition: Things that are natural are not made by people.
words.example: We need to take care of the natural world.

words.definition: Nowadays means at the present time.
words.example: Nowadays, not so many people smoke.

words.definition: A participant is someone who joins in a social event or competition.
words.example: There were thousands of participants in this year’s marathon.

words.definition: A ritual is a formal custom that people do regularly.
words.example: Ken was very interested to learn about the religious rituals of the natives.

words.definition: Spoken language is what we say.
words.example: We cannot take back what has been spoken.

words.definition: Sport involves games like running, jumping, football, and tennis.
words.example: She loves watching sport on TV.

words.definition: You are surprised when something unexpected happens.
words.example: He didn’t appear at all surprised when he read the article.

words.definition: When you are tense, you are not comfortable and feel unhappy.
words.example: I felt very tense waiting to hear the result of the vote.

words.definition: If you totally agree, you agree with everything just said.
words.example: I am totally against that.

words.definition: If something is vague, it is not clear and gives very few details.
words.example: I asked him about his mother’s health, but he was very vague about it.

words.definition: To allow something to happen means to let it happen.
words.example: Having a ticket will allow you to enter the show.

words.definition: To announce something is to make it known.
words.example: He announced to everyone his new idea for the company.

words.definition: Someone or something beside you is next to you.
words.example: The two brothers stood beside each other.

words.definition: A challenge is something difficult to complete.
words.example: It was a challenge to climb to the top of the mountain.

words.definition: To claim means to say that something is true.
words.example: He claimed to know why the country’s laws were weak.

words.definition: The condition of someone or something is the state that they are in.
words.example: The patient’s condition was very good.

words.definition: To contribute to something means to do something to make it successful.
words.example: We decided to contribute money to the new hospital.

words.definition: A difference is a way that something is not like other things.
words.example: The biggest difference between the birds is the color of their feathers.

words.definition: To divide something is to split it into smaller parts.
words.example: We divided the pizza.

words.definition: An expert is someone who is very good at doing something.
words.example: The wizard was an expert at magic.

words.definition: A famous person or thing is well known.
words.example: The Eiffel Tower in Paris is very famous.

words.definition: Force is a person’s strength or power.
words.example: He used all his force to try and open the door.

words.definition: To cause harm is to hurt someone or damage something.
words.example: A hot iron can cause great harm if you are not careful.

words.definition: To lay means to put or place in a horizontal or flat position.
words.example: Don’t lay your socks on the floor.

words.definition: Peace is a time without war.
words.example: A white dove is a symbol of peace.

words.definition: A prince is the son of a king.
words.example: The prince and the princess were married.

words.definition: To protect someone is to stop them from getting hurt.
words.example: Firemen protect us from fires.

words.definition: To sense something is to know about it without being told.
words.example: I could sense that he was watching me.

words.definition: When something is sudden, it happens very quickly.
words.example: He felt a sudden pain in his chest.

words.definition: Therefore means for this reason.
words.example: He is fat. Therefore, he should go on a diet.

words.definition: To accept something that is offered is to take it.
words.example: I accepted the girl’s very nice gift.

words.definition: To arrange things is to put them in the right place.
words.example: Please arrange the words in order from A to Z.

words.definition: To attend something is to go to it.
words.example: My sister and I attend the same school.

words.definition: You chase people when you run after them and try to catch them.
words.example: I was chased by a dog.

words.definition: A contrast is a sharp difference between two things.
words.example: The contrast between my parents is very noticeable.

words.definition: To encourage people is to make them want to do something.
words.example: My football coach will encourage us when we are losing.

words.definition: People or things familiar to you are those you know well.
words.example: The two friends were very familiar with each other.

words.definition: To grab is to take a hold of someone or something suddenly.
words.example: I grabbed a pear from the tree.

words.definition: To hang something is to keep it above the ground.
words.example: I drew a picture of my family, and my mother hung it on the wall.

words.definition: If something is huge, it is very big.
words.example: At work, my father drives a huge truck.

words.definition: If something is necessary, you must do it.
words.example: A passport is necessary if you travel to other countries.

words.definition: A pattern is a way in which something is done or organized.
words.example: My pattern of brushing my teeth is the same as most people’s.

words.definition: To propose something is to say that it should be done.
words.example: My grandmother proposed that we have our picture taken with Santa.

words.definition: A purpose is the reason that you do something.
words.example: The purpose of exercising is to get into shape.

words.definition: To release something is to stop holding it.
words.example: She released the bird from her hands.

words.definition: To require something is to say that it is necessary.
words.example: We require teachers to have a university degree.

words.definition: You are satisfied when you have what you wanted.
words.example: I am very satisfied with your work.

words.definition: If something is single, then there is only one.
words.example: I have a single key in my hand.

words.definition: To tear something means to pull it apart.
words.example: It is easy to tear paper.

words.definition: A theory is an idea about how something works.
words.example: We talked about Einstein’s theory of relativity in class.

words.definition: An animal is a living thing that can move.
words.example: My favorite animal is the panda.

words.definition: A bus is a large vehicle that people travel on.
words.example: My father takes the bus to work.

words.definition: A cat is a small animal related to lions and tigers that is kept as a pet.
words.example: This cat is playing with a ball.

words.definition: A command is an order given to a person or animal to do something.
words.example: Joe gave the students a command to stand up.

words.definition: To depend on something is to need it for support or help.
words.example: My grandfather depends on a cane when he walks.

words.definition: A dog is an animal with four legs and a tail that is kept as a pet or trained to work.
words.example: This woman’s best friend is her dog.

words.definition: A door is an object that swings or slides open and shut.
words.example: Can you close the door, please?

words.definition: A friend is someone a person knows and likes spending time with.
words.example: Brian’s friend is very sad.

words.definition: To hear is to be aware of sound through your ears.
words.example: Michelle cannot hear what you are saying.

words.definition: To help is to do something that makes something easier for someone else.
words.example: Jane can help Nathan climb up the rock.

words.definition: A horse is a big, strong animal that people ride and use for pulling heavy things.
words.example: I went to a farm and saw a horse.

words.definition: A hospital is where sick or hurt people receive care or treatment.
words.example: The doctor talks to a patient at the hospital.

words.definition: A leg is a body part used for standing and walking.
words.example: She hurt her leg.

words.definition: Medical means related to the treatment of an injury or disease.
words.example: Tyler is a medical student studying to become a doctor.

words.definition: To open is to move something so that an opening is not covered.
words.example: Amy likes to open the window to let fresh air in.

words.definition: To pull is to hold onto something to move it toward you.
words.example: The children pull the rope.

words.definition: A rabbit is a small animal with long ears that lives in a hole in the ground.
words.example: Look at the rabbit in the park.

words.definition: A school is a place where children go to learn.
words.example: The students study at school.

words.definition: To see is to use your eyes to look at something or someone.
words.example: Steven does not want to see the scary picture.

words.definition: Service is the act of helping or serving someone.
words.example: This coffee shop has excellent service.

words.definition: A benefit is a good thing.
words.example: Being able to fly is a benefit to birds.

words.definition: If you are certain about something, you know it is true.
words.example: I am certain that zebras have stripes.

words.definition: A chance is an opportunity to do something.
words.example: I had a chance to see the Coliseum in Rome last summer.

words.definition: An effect is a change made by something else.
words.example: The medicine had a good effect on the boy.

words.definition: If something is essential, it is very important and necessary.
words.example: It is essential to have oxygen when you scuba dive.

words.definition: If something is far, it is not close.
words.example: It’s far from the east coast to the west coast of America.

words.definition: To focus on something is to think about it and pay attention to it.
words.example: My mom always helps me to focus on my school work.

words.definition: The function of something is what it does.
words.example: The function of a flashlight is to help you see in the dark.

words.definition: Grass is the green leaves that cover the ground.
words.example: The grass looked so soft and green.

words.definition: To guard something is to take care of it.
words.example: The police officer will guard us from any harm.

words.definition: The image of something is a picture of it.
words.example: The image of her eye was very clear.

words.definition: If something is immediate, it happens quickly.
words.example: An immediate response came from the pizza place.

words.definition: If something is primary, it is the most important thing.
words.example: His primary thoughts are about money.

words.definition: People who feel proud are happy about what they have done.
words.example: She is proud of the picture she drew of her house.

words.definition: To remain somewhere is to stay there.
words.example: My sister had to remain home since she was sick.

words.definition: To rest is to stop being active while the body gets back its strength.
words.example: I rested on the couch after work.

words.definition: If two things are separate, they are not together.
words.example: New York and Los Angeles are in two separate parts of America.

words.definition: A site is a place.
words.example: We found the perfect site for our picnic.

words.definition: A tail is a part of an animal’s body that sticks out from its rear or back.
words.example: Our dog wags its tail when it’s happy.

words.definition: Trouble is a problem or a difficulty.
words.example: I have trouble working with my boss.

words.definition: To advertise is to describe or draw attention to a product or event by using a public medium.
words.example: The woman started a new company and needed to advertise her products.

words.definition: If someone is aware, they know that something or a situation exists.
words.example: The student became aware that the teacher was watching him.

words.definition: A battery is an object placed inside something to supply it with electricity.
words.example: My brother needs a battery for his clock.

words.definition: Black is the darkest color.
words.example: Our street is black at night because there are no street lights.

words.definition: A city is a place where a lot of people live.
words.example: Tokyo is a very big city in Japan.

words.definition: To clean is to make something neat and tidy.
words.example: I clean our kitchen every Saturday.

words.definition: A country is an area of land with the same government and laws.
words.example: France is a country in Europe.

words.definition: To develop is to make something larger or more advanced.
words.example: This practice will help you develop your math skills.

words.definition: If something is electric, it uses electricity.
words.example: Some car companies make electric cars.

words.definition: When something happens at a later time or in the end, it happens eventually.
words.example: He will eventually move to London to find a new job.

words.definition: A fact is a piece of information that is true.
words.example: A fact about South America is that it is a continent.

words.definition: Glass is a transparent, breakable material.
words.example: Windows are made of glass.

words.definition: History is the study of the past.
words.example: History was my favorite subject in school.

words.definition: Nature is everything in the physical world that is not made by people.
words.example: On the weekends, I love to walk in nature among the trees.

words.definition: Never is when something is impossible or will not happen.
words.example: They never eat meat because they are vegetarians.

words.definition: People are humans.
words.example: How many people live in China?

words.definition: Plastic is a material made by people.
words.example: Many drinks are sold in plastic bottles.

words.definition: A problem is a situation when something goes wrong.
words.example: My problem is that I lost my dog.

words.definition: A street is a road in a city or village.
words.example: What is the name of the street you live on?

words.definition: To think is to have an opinion or thought about something.
words.example: I think summer is the best season.

words.definition: A person who is alone is not with another person.
words.example: The boy wanted to be alone to think.

words.definition: An apartment is a set of rooms in a building where people live.
words.example: She has a nice apartment in the city.

words.definition: An article is a story in a newspaper or magazine.
words.example: Did you read the article in the newspaper about the soccer game?

words.definition: An artist is a person who paints, draws, or makes sculptures.
words.example: He went to Paris to become an artist.

words.definition: Someone’s attitude is the way they feel and think.
words.example: John has a bad attitude. He’s always angry.

words.definition: Beauty is the state or quality of being beautiful.
words.example: I heard my mother was a great beauty when she was young.

words.definition: To compare means to say how two things are the same and different.
words.example: If you compare cats and dogs, you’ll see that they’re both good pets.

words.definition: To judge something is to say if it is good or bad.
words.example: The boy was going to judge how his mother’s turkey tasted.

words.definition: A magazine is a regular publication with news, stories, and articles.
words.example: She likes to read fashion magazines.

words.definition: A material is what is used to make something.
words.example: Brick is a good material for building houses.

words.definition: A meal is a time when food is eaten, such as breakfast, lunch, or dinner.
words.example: Breakfast is my favorite meal because I enjoy cereal.

words.definition: A method is the way to do something.
words.example: One method to remember things is to tie a string around your finger.

words.definition: A neighbor is a person who lives near you.
words.example: I like my neighbor because he’s very friendly.

words.definition: If something is professional, it deals with work that uses special skills.
words.example: If you want to be a pilot, you must have professional training.

words.definition: A profit is the extra money you make when you sell something.
words.example: I made a small profit from selling my old clothes.

words.definition: The quality of something is how good it is.
words.example: The quality of his car is very good.

words.definition: A space is an empty area.
words.example: I don’t have much space for things in my small house.

words.definition: Stairs are the things that are used to walk up or down in a building.
words.example: You can take the stairs to the second floor.

words.definition: A symbol is a thing that stands for something else.
words.example: This symbol tells us that we cannot smoke in this area.

words.definition: If someone or something is thin, they are not fat.
words.example: The man was thin because he didn’t eat much.

words.definition: People study accounting so they can deal with money and finance properly.
words.example: He works for an accounting firm.

words.example: The citizens all signed a petition asking the mayor to repair the sidewalks.

words.definition: To renovate a building means to repair it, or to build new structures on it.
words.example: The old fire station was renovated into an apartment building.

words.definition: To revise something means to change it, or update it to make it better.
words.example: When the editor discovered certain facts were wrong, he revised the book.

words.definition: A slab is a large, thick, flat piece of stone, concrete, metal, or wood.
words.example: I looked at various slabs of stone to decorate my house.

words.definition: A terrace is an open area that is connected to a house or an apartment.
words.example: In the afternoons, she liked to sit on the terrace and check her email.

words.definition: Turf is a section of grass and the dirt in which it grows.
words.example: After the game, the turf looked ragged.

words.definition: If something is analogous to another thing, then it is like it in certain ways.
words.example: The relationship with his teacher was analogous to that of a son and mother.

words.definition: Binoculars are a device used for seeing things that are far away.
words.example: He could see the ship on the horizon only if he used his binoculars.

words.definition: The bulk of something is its size.
words.example: The large elephant moved its bulk with legs as strong as tree trunks.

words.definition: If something comprises something else, it consists of or is made up of it.
words.example: Our school’s football team is mostly comprised with seniors.

words.definition: To depict something means to show or portray it, often using art.
words.example: The statue’s face depicted the general’s determination and courage.

words.definition: If something is dual, then it is made up of two parts.
words.example: The room had a dual function. It was a living room, but at night it was a bedroom.

words.definition: Fahrenheit is a temperature scale where water freezes at 32° and boils at 212°.
words.example: When the temperature dropped to 32° Fahrenheit, it started snowing.

words.definition: To fulfill something means to achieve or finish it.
words.example: The professor did not fulfill his promise not to miss a single class.

words.definition: A grove is a small group of trees.
words.example: All the trees in this grove are apple trees.

words.definition: Ore is the raw form of rock or material from which a valuable metal is taken.
words.example: The factory melted the ore and used it to make iron products.

words.definition: The outback is the wild inland region of Australia where very few people live.
words.example: Many Australian farmers use the outback to raise cattle.

words.definition: To outweigh something means to exceed it in value, amount, or importance.
words.example: Finding a warm place to sleep outweighed the need to find something to eat.

words.definition: A paradox is a true statement or real event that seems illogical.
words.example: The paradox of her work was that the less she worked, the more she got done.

words.definition: A pier is a structure that extends into a body of water.
words.example: If you want to catch bigger fish, then go to the far end of the pier.

words.definition: A shortcut is a route that is shorter than the main route.
words.example: We got to the house early because we took a shortcut through the forest.

words.definition: A tariff is a tax or fee paid on certain imports or exports.
words.example: Our tariff on imported wool makes foreign wool more expensive.

words.definition: A thermometer is a device that measures temperature.
words.example: The thermometer outside the window indicated that it was a hot day today.

words.definition: To tilt something means to tip it into a sloping position.
words.example: She tilted her glass and almost spilled some of the wine inside.

words.definition: If a statement is vice versa, then its two main ideas are switched with one another.
words.example: Students learn from their teachers, and vice versa.

words.definition: The whereabouts of someone or something is the place where they are.
words.example: The police looked for the lost dog, but its whereabouts were still unknown.
